events.title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT as a free research preview
events.place: OpenAI headquarters, Mission District, San Francisco, California
events.summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT, a GPT-3.5-based model that 'interacts in a conversational way', as a research preview that was free to use at chat.openai.com. Every conversation typed into it was, by default, text a company could log and learn from.
events.significance: The mass-market chatbot turned ordinary people's questions, drafts and confidences into training and product data at a scale no privacy notice had anticipated, and set up the assistants that became agents.

sources.institution: OpenAI (archived by the Internet Archive Wayback Machine, capture of 30 November 2022)
sources.title: ChatGPT: Optimizing Language Models for Dialogue
sources.quote: We are excited to introduce ChatGPT to get users' feedback and learn about its strengths and weaknesses. During the research preview, usage of ChatGPT is free.
sources.note: openai.com returns HTTP 403 to scripts; quote checked on the Wayback capture made on the day of release (30 Nov 2022 18:09 UTC).

events.locationNote: Online release; mapped to OpenAI's then headquarters (Pioneer Building, 18th Street, San Francisco).

events.title: Italy's data-protection authority orders an immediate limit on ChatGPT
events.place: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali, Piazza Venezia 11, Rome
events.summary: By urgent order no. 112 of 30 March 2023, announced on 31 March, the Italian Garante imposed a temporary limitation on OpenAI's processing of data of people in Italy. It found no information notice to users or data subjects, no adequate legal basis for collecting personal data to train ChatGPT's algorithms, inaccurate outputs about people, and no age verification. OpenAI was given 20 days to report its remedies on pain of a fine of up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide turnover.
events.significance: The first regulator to stop a general-purpose chatbot did so on privacy grounds, establishing that training and running AI on people's data needs a lawful basis the person can see.

sources.institution: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italian Data Protection Authority)
sources.title: Provvedimento del 30 marzo 2023 [doc. web n. 9870832] (Registro dei provvedimenti n. 112)
sources.quote: RILEVATA l’assenza di idonea base giuridica in relazione alla raccolta dei dati personali e al loro trattamento per scopo di addestramento degli algoritmi sottesi al funzionamento di ChatGPT;
sources.note: Italian original. Translation: 'NOTING the absence of a suitable legal basis for the collection of personal data and their processing for the purpose of training the algorithms underlying the operation of ChatGPT'.

sources.institution: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italian Data Protection Authority)
sources.title: Artificial intelligence: stop to ChatGPT by the Italian SA. Personal data is collected unlawfully, no age verification system is in place for children (press release, doc. web n. 9870847)
sources.quote: The Italian SA imposed an immediate temporary limitation on the processing of Italian users’ data by OpenAI, the US-based company developing and managing the platform. An inquiry into the facts of the case was initiated as well.

events.locationNote: Seat of the Garante, Piazza Venezia, Rome.

events.title: Garante fines OpenAI EUR 15 million over ChatGPT (later overturned in court)
events.place: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali, Piazza Venezia 11, Rome
events.summary: Closing its ChatGPT inquiry with decision no. 755 of 2 November 2024, announced on 20 December 2024, the Garante fined OpenAI EUR 15 million and ordered a six-month information campaign on radio, TV, newspapers and the internet. It found OpenAI had trained ChatGPT on users' personal data without first identifying a legal basis, breached transparency duties, failed to notify a March 2023 breach and lacked age verification. The Garante's own page now records that the Court of Rome, in judgment no. 4153/2026 published on 18 March 2026, upheld OpenAI's appeal, and the decision was removed from the site.
events.significance: It shows both the reach and the fragility of after-the-fact enforcement: a record fine for training on personal data, then annulled on appeal more than a year later.

sources.institution: Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italian Data Protection Authority)
sources.title: ChatGPT, The Italian Data Protection Authority closes the preliminary investigation. OpenAI will have to carry out a six-month information campaign and pay a fine of EUR 15 million (press release, doc. web n. 10085432)
sources.quote: The Data Protection Authority imposed a fine of EUR 15 million on OpenAI, which was also calculated taking into account the company’s cooperative attitude.
sources.note: The same page carries the later notice: 'Decision No. 755 of 2 November 2024 has been temporarily removed from the website of the Italian Data Protection Authority following judgment No. 4153/2026 of the Court of Rome. The judgment, published on 18 March 2026, upheld the appeal lodged against the Authority’s decision'. The judgment itself was not read.
